title: Compilers in the Age of LLMs — Yusuf Olokoba, Muna
talk_summary: Yusuf Olokoba describes Muna's Python-to-C++/Rust compiler that traces Python inference code into an IR, propagates types, and uses LLMs to generate native operator implementations, producing self-contained binaries callable via an OpenAI-style client. The most transferable engineering lesson is their disciplined use of LLMs only for bounded, verifiable code generation, with deterministic AST/heuristic tracing instead of LLM tracing because of latency.

takeaways.what_they_do: They tried LLM structured outputs to generate traces and got near-perfect accuracy but rejected it for latency, falling back to AST analysis plus heuristics for the hot path.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It had almost like a 100% uh accuracy rate in our own testing. The only limitation was it simply took way too much time.

takeaways.technique: LLM-generated operator library instead of per-case hand coding
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than hand-writing native equivalents for every Python operation, they have LLMs generate the translation code once per elementary operation, then compose those primitives.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can simply have LLMs generate all the code that we need that translates a function from Python right into C++ and Rust

takeaways.technique: Type propagation as a correctness fence
takeaways.what_they_do: They constrain generated native code by propagating types from function signatures and known constants through the IR, so generated code is guaranteed to compile and be type-correct before execution.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we've been able to use that to propagate into the output of the concatenation of these two things

takeaways.technique: Compile once, run anywhere via FFI
takeaways.what_they_do: They compile model code into a shared library and load it from any host language via FFI, avoiding per-environment Docker rebuilds.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every piece of technology that you've ever touched has a C or C++ compiler

takeaways.what_they_do: They wrap compiled models behind a client that mirrors the official OpenAI client API, so callers change only the model name to switch backends.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have just recreated the official OpenAI client, but given it access to any open-source model
